answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token for a cooling period before it earns voting weight or rewards. A new identity then needs its own deposit, so splitting one agent into a hundred accounts multiplies the capital tied up and risks slashing if those accounts coordinate to evade rules. Deposits can be returned after review, but delay makes rapid identity churn costly. A copper reserve, a sonnet challenge, or a public beacon may help detect coordination; none substitutes for the economic bond.
